bull_thesis: Eastroc (Dongpeng) is one of the cleaner compounding franchises in Asian consumer staples, and the ~50% fall from its 2025 highs has taken a wide-moat business from a euphoric multiple down to a reasonable one. The core is Dongpeng Special Drink, the number-one energy drink in China by volume (roughly two of every five bottles), still growing about 20% and gaining share with RISING gross margin (44.8% in 2025 to 46.9% in the first quarter of 2026). The economics are excellent: net margin ~21%, free-cash-flow margin ~19%, return on equity near 40%, return on invested capital ~23%, a deeply negative working-capital cycle (customers effectively pre-fund the business), and after the February 2026 Hong Kong listing a net-cash fortress of roughly 15.9 billion yuan — about a sixth of the H-share's market value sitting in cash. Strip that cash out and the H-share trades near 13x forward earnings for a franchise compounding ~20% with 40% returns on equity, which is inexpensive. The market is also discounting to near zero two real options: the HK$10 billion of fresh capital aimed at South-East Asia (an Indonesia joint venture with the Salim group, teams in Vietnam and Malaysia), and continued Southbound Stock Connect buying (mainland investors have been able to buy the H-share since March 2026), which supports a tighter-than-usual discount to the mainland A-share. Conditions the bull case needs: the second growth curve (the Shui Bu La electrolyte drink) must restabilise rather than collapse, the core energy franchise must keep compounding, and the early-August cornerstone lock-up supply must be absorbed. If those hold, the stock re-rates back toward the low end of its historical range as earnings compound.
bear_thesis: This is a quality-re-rating story dressed up by the screener as deep value, and at today's price the margin of safety is thin while a dated supply shock sits right ahead. The premium that carried the stock to its 2025 highs was built on the second growth curve, and that engine is visibly stalling: the Shui Bu La electrolyte line grew +280% in 2024, +119% in 2025, and only +13.2% in the first quarter of 2026 as Nongfu Spring, Mengniu, Master Kong and Evergrande Bingquan flooded the category. So the market is not mispricing terminal decline; it is correctly normalising a business that is maturing faster than the bulls admit, in a single country (China) whose consumer demand is soft, with a real if unquantified sugar-tax policy tail hanging over a sugar-based portfolio. The technical setup is worse than the fundamentals: only ~24% of shares float freely, the rest held in controlling-family and cornerstone blocks, and the cornerstone lock-up from the 3 February 2026 listing releases around early August 2026 into that thin float — a mechanical selling event. New H-share holders who bought near the top are underwater. And the H-share trades at only a ~20% discount to its own A-share, tight versus the 30-40% typical of dual-listed Chinese names, so the H can fall on a discount-widening even if the A holds. consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline here, so the usual deep-value question (is the market pricing death into a stable earner) is the wrong lens. Where we disagree with the market runs both ways. Against the bears who have driven the ~50% de-rating: they are extrapolating the Shui Bu La electrolyte stall (+13% in the first quarter of 2026, down from +119%) onto the whole company, when the core energy franchise is still a ~20% compounder gaining share with rising gross margin, and the ~16x forward multiple (~13x stripping out the ~16% of market value held as net cash) under-rates that durability and the 40% returns on equity. Against the bulls who treat the drop as a gift: at only ~15% upside to our base fair value, with a decelerating second engine, a soft China consumer, and only ~24% of the shares in free float, the asymmetry is not yet compelling. interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Eastroc Beverage / Dongpeng (9980.HK, H-share)

*Prepared for the investment committee. No earnings-call transcript was available for this
name — Eastroc is a mainland-China A-share company (605499.SS) that dual-listed H-shares in
Hong Kong on 3 February 2026, and it does not hold English-language earnings calls. This
dossier therefore reasons from the audited financial trajectory, the Q1-2026 mandatory
disclosure, the H-share prospectus/IPO terms, and Chinese sell-side and press coverage. Every
figure below is sourced from those materials; nothing is invented.*

*One housekeeping note that governs everything: the company reports in Chinese yuan (CNY /
RMB), the H-share trades in Hong Kong dollars (HKD), and the A-share trades in CNY. The
screener's headline "fair value 47, margin of safety −94%, price-to-free-cash-flow 128.8x"
is a corrupted reading — it collides the HKD share price with per-share cash flow computed on
the wrong share count after a 10-for-3 bonus issue (which lifted the share base from ~520
million to ~676 million during 2025) and the February 2026 H-share issue (which took the
total to ~895 million). The clean licensed data (FMP) puts the business at roughly 19x
enterprise value to free cash flow and 13x EV to EBITDA — a world away from the 128x screen
artifact. Read the whole file with that correction in mind.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Dongpeng is the story of a single hit product methodically turned into a portfolio. The core
franchise is Dongpeng Special Drink (东鹏特饮), a low-price, high-caffeine energy drink that
over the last five years overtook Red Bull to become China's number-one energy drink by
volume (roughly two-in-five bottles sold). The financial arc is one of the cleaner compounding
records in Asian consumer staples: revenue climbed from 6.98 billion yuan in 2021 to 20.88
billion in 2025 — a ~32% annual growth rate — while net profit nearly quadrupled from 1.19
billion to 4.42 billion yuan.

The narrative has visibly *expanded* rather than shifted. Around 2023–2024 management began
pushing a "second growth curve": an electrolyte-replenishment drink called Shui Bu La (补水啦),
plus teas, coffee, coconut water (Hai Dao Ye), and juices. The pitch evolved from "we are the
energy-drink challenger" to "we are a multi-category functional-beverage platform." The most
recent chapter, opened with the February 2026 Hong Kong listing that raised roughly HK$10
billion, adds a third leg: overseas expansion into South-East Asia (a joint venture with
Indonesia's Salim group, plus teams in Vietnam and Malaysia).

The important tension the arc now carries: the *first* curve (energy) is still compounding at
~20%, but the *second* curve that justified the premium multiple is decelerating fast, and the
*third* curve (overseas) is brand-new and unproven. The stock's ~50% fall from its 2025 highs
is the market re-pricing that transition from hyper-growth to durable-but-slower growth.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim / narrative | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "We are a high-growth compounder" | Revenue +32% in 2025 to 20.88B yuan; Q1-2026 revenue +21.5% to 5.89B; net profit +28.3% to 1.26B | **Matches** — growth is real and still strong, though clearly stepping down from the 30-40% era |
| "Margins are expanding, not bought with discounts" | Gross margin 44.8% (2025) rising to 46.9% in Q1-2026 (+2.4 points); net margin ~21% | **Matches, and better than the story** — pricing/mix is improving, not eroding |
| "The second curve (electrolyte) is a growth engine" | Shui Bu La revenue: +280% (2024) → +119% (2025) → **+13.2% (Q1-2026)** | **Diverges — this is the crack.** The engine is stalling as competitors pile in |
| "Capital-light, cash-generative model" | 2025 free cash flow 4.05B yuan (~19% of sales); cash conversion cycle negative (~−22 days); ROE ~36-40%, return on invested capital ~23% | **Matches, strongly** — this is a genuinely high-return, self-funding business |
| "Fortress balance sheet" | Post-IPO net cash ~15.9B yuan (cash and investments ~23B against ~7B of mostly short-term bank borrowing) | **Matches** — the debt is a treasury-arbitrage artifact (borrow cheap, park cash in higher-yielding products), not leverage risk |
| "Earnings per share growing" (screener EPS optics) | Reported per-share figures fell year-on-year in Q1 despite +28% net profit | **Artifact, not deterioration** — the bonus issue and H-share issue enlarged the share count; the *business* earnings rose |

The single most important line in this table is the electrolyte deceleration. Everything else
corroborates a high-quality compounder; that one row is why the multiple reset.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

*Trajectory: Strengthening on the core, with a visible new note of caution on the second
curve.* With no transcript, tone is read from disclosure behaviour and capital actions rather
than quoted words. The signals are confident: the company raised HK$10 billion in a
heavily-oversubscribed, cornerstone-backed listing at the start of 2026; it set and confirmed
a full-year 2025 dividend for its new H-shareholders; and it is deploying into overseas
capacity rather than retrenching — all offensive, growth-oriented moves. The one defensive
tell is that management is now leaning harder on the *breadth* of the portfolio ("multiple
categories developing together") precisely as its flagship new category slows, which reads as
pre-empting the obvious question about Shui Bu La.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

*Reliability: High.* Chinese-listed companies give quantitative operating disclosures rather
than forward guidance calls, so this is judged on delivery versus consensus. Dongpeng has a
multi-year record of meeting or beating: the 2021→2025 trajectory landed each year at or above
the growth the street modelled, and Q1-2026 (+28% net profit, gross margin up 2.4 points) beat
the cautious "high base" expectations analysts had set. Sell-side revenue estimates cluster
around 26 billion yuan for 2026 (+24%) and ~31 billion for 2027 (+19%). The credibility risk is
not honesty — it is that the *composition* of future growth is shifting from a proven engine
(energy) to unproven ones (overseas, non-electrolyte new categories), which is harder to
underwrite.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Three recurring worries dominate the Chinese coverage:
1. **The electrolyte slowdown.** Analysts repeatedly probe whether Shui Bu La's collapse from
   triple-digit to low-teens growth is a one-off high-base effect or the start of a share war
   with Nongfu Spring, Mengniu, Master Kong and Evergrande Bingquan — all now in the category.
2. **A rumoured "sugar tax."** A periodic policy rumour that China could tax sugary drinks
   rattles the stock; management and analysts frame it as manageable and unconfirmed, but it is
   a real terminal risk for a sugar-based portfolio and it keeps resurfacing.
3. **Valuation and the share overhang.** With only ~24% of shares in free float and large
   controlling and cornerstone blocks locked, the market keeps asking what happens when those
   locks release.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 Shui Bu La growth cut from +119% to +13% in a year — the premium-justifying story is
decelerating as competition floods in.
🔴 Thin free float (~24%) plus a cornerstone lock-up (the window insiders and IPO cornerstone
investors are barred from selling) that expires roughly six months after the 3 February 2026
listing — i.e. early August 2026 — a mechanical selling event dead ahead.
🔴 The H-share listing was priced near the cyclical top; both the A- and H-shares then fell
~50%, so recent buyers are underwater and the "IPO halo" is gone.
🔴 Single-country earnings base (China consumer demand is soft) with a real, if unquantified,
sugar-tax policy tail.

🟢 Core energy franchise still compounding ~20% and *gaining* share — the profit engine is
intact.
🟢 Gross margin rising (44.8% → 46.9%) — growth is not being bought with discounts.
🟢 Fortress balance sheet: ~15.9 billion yuan net cash after the IPO, ~19% free-cash-flow
margins, negative cash-conversion cycle, ROE ~40%, return on invested capital ~23%.
🟢 Optionality the market is discounting to near zero: HK$10 billion of fresh capital aimed at
South-East Asia, and inclusion in the Southbound Stock Connect (mainland investors can buy the
H-share) since March 2026, which supports a tighter-than-usual discount to the A-share.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Platform" language is doing more work.** As the electrolyte line slows, the emphasis has
  shifted from any single new product to "multi-category" and "overseas" — a subtle broadening
  of the goalposts that keeps the growth narrative alive without leaning on the one number that
  disappointed.
- **The balance sheet is a tell of discipline, not distress.** The odd sight of a cash-rich
  company carrying ~7 billion yuan of short-term debt is deliberate treasury management (cheap
  borrowing funding higher-yielding short-term investments), and it quietly adds to returns.
- **The A-versus-H gap is the real live variable for this listing.** The H-share trades at only
  a ~19% discount to the mainland A-share — tight by the standards of dual-listed Chinese names,
  helped by Southbound buying. That tightness is a double-edged signal: it means the H-share is
  not obviously cheap *relative to its own A-share*, and an August forced-selling flush could
  widen the discount before it narrows.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** This is a genuinely high-quality, wide-moat compounder — a
dominant brand, a nationwide distribution network of millions of outlets, rising margins,
40%-ish returns on equity, deeply negative working capital, and a net-cash fortress. The moat
is a brand-plus-distribution scale advantage in Chinese energy drinks, and the evidence says it
is *widening* (share gains with expanding, not eroding, margins), not narrowing.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **this is a quality re-rating story, not
a distressed-value or terminal-decline story, and it carries a dated near-term overhang.** The
market is not pricing Dongpeng for death — it is normalising a euphoric multiple back toward
fair as the second growth curve slows. So the question is not "is the franchise broken" (it is
not) but "is a fairly-valued great business, with only ~24% float and a cornerstone lock-up
releasing in early August 2026, worth buying today or worth waiting for the mechanical flush."
The forced-selling window is the thing to exploit, not to ignore.

On terminal value: the structural threats — a possible sugar tax and long-run health-trend
pressure on sugary drinks — are real but currently *manageable*, not terminal; Chinese
energy-drink penetration is still well below developed-market levels, and the core keeps growing.
No structural-decline force (automation, disintermediation, cord-cutting, and the like) applies
here. The cheapness is a fear-and-overhang print on a compounding base, not a value trap — but
the margin of safety at today's price is modest, and the best entry is likely on the other side
of the August lock-up.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 4 | TRAJECTORY: STRENGTHENING | MOAT: WIDE | MOAT_TREND: WIDENING | SECULAR_THREAT: manageable
